## Expected Behavior `net/url.Parse` should be considered deterministic ## Actual Behavior `net/url.Parse` call in a workflow is considered non-determenistic due to the underlying calls to the GC.
Output of go run go.temporal.io/sdk/contrib/tools/workflowcheck@efbe53f6247023120bcbe69a6258682e6d1c0d2c -v ./main.go ``` 11:57:56.346104 load [./main.go] 11:57:57.283251 building graph of analysis passes /tmp/bad-url/main.go:13:14: (*command-line-arguments.wf).ParseURL is non-deterministic, reason: calls non-deterministic function net/url.Parse net/url.Parse is non-deterministic, reason: calls ## Steps to Reproduce the Problem Run `workflowcheck` (latest as of opening this issue: `v0.4.1-0.20260213005113-efbe53f62470`) on a minimal workflow application:
main.go ```go package main import ( "net/url" "go.temporal.io/sdk/client" "go.temporal.io/sdk/worker" "go.temporal.io/sdk/workflow" ) type wf struct{} func (w *wf) ParseURL(workflow.Context) (*url.URL, error) { return url.Parse("https://github.com") } func main() { c, err := client.NewLazyClient(client.Options{}) if err != nil { panic(err) } defer c.Close() wfWorker := worker.New(c, "testing", worker.Options{}) urlWorker := &wf{} wfWorker.RegisterActivity(urlWorker.ParseURL) } ```

comments.body: :+1: This was due to https://github.com/golang/go/commit/ff654ea. We found other Go 1.26 issues in #2188 too. Will address both soon.
